content: Jacqui Jackson is a single parent raising seven children, which includes three adolescent daughters and four sons. All four of her sons are on the autism spectrum. In 2003, Jackson and her family were featured in a BBC documentary titled My Family and Autism. Later, in 2005, BBC Two aired a drama called Magnificent 7, in which Helena Bonham Carter portrayed a character named Maggi, who was based on Jacqui Jackson. Jackson resides in Blackpool, Lancashire, England. Family Life Jacqui Jackson's sons are as follows: Matthew: He is the eldest child in the family. Matthew was born prematurely and has been diagnosed with dyslexia and developmental dyspraxia. Luke: He has been diagnosed with Asperger syndrome and dyspraxia. At the age of 13, Luke authored a book titled Freaks, Geeks and Asperger's Syndrome, which details his experiences living with the condition. Joe: He has been diagnosed with ADHD. Ben: He is the youngest child in the family. Ben was born prematurely and is autistic. In addition to her four sons, Jacqui Jackson has three daughters named Rachel, Sarah, and Anna. Education Jacqui Jackson holds a first-class honours degree in social science from the Open University. She is currently pursuing a PhD at Coventry University, focusing on sensory issues in autistic children.
